National Parliament
National Assembly
Twenty-first Session
Complete Minutes of Proceedings
5 Bhadra 2083
Friday
Meeting Number- 49
The National Assembly meeting today commenced at 1:21 PM under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Chairperson Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable members, the agenda for today's National Assembly meeting (1:23 PM) begins. Honourable members, names have been received to speak during Zero Hour. I will now provide time for the Honourable members to speak.
First, Honourable Member Krishna Bahadur Rokaya.
Honourable Mr. Krishna Bahadur Rokaya (Nepali Congress):- Honourable Chairperson, due to floods and landslides, the recent incidents in Jajarkot, Rolpa, and Bajura, along with other incidents across the country, have claimed the lives of approximately 267 people. Similarly, due to continuous rainfall on the 39th of Shrawan, landslides in Seri village of ward 5 of Rukum Paschim Municipality put the houses of Vanita Malla, Hari Bahadur Sunar, and Hem Bahadur Pandey at high risk, and they have been moved to a safe location, while 10 other houses are at risk. Due to continuous rainfall on the night of the 2nd of Bhadra, landslides in ward 14 of Musikot Municipality have damaged the houses of Kripa Khadka, Lal Bahadur Khadka, and Yuvraj Khadka, who are taking shelter with relatives. The settlement itself is at high risk of landslides. Honourable Chairperson, I draw the attention of the Nepal Government through the Right Honourable Chairperson to send a special team from the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority to the aforementioned high-risk settlements immediately to assess the damage and arrange for relief and rehabilitation for the affected. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Ghanashyam Rizal.
Honourable Mr. Ghanashyam Rizal (Nepali Communist Party):- Honourable Chairperson, Deepa Nepali, who was evicted from her rented room based on her caste, and many other Dalit youth students like Rup Sunar and Karuna Bishwakarma, who have faced discrimination, have not received justice even from the courts regarding issues of caste discrimination. Deepa Nepali has been on a hunger strike for a long time, saying "Room Available, Government." This is not just the hunger strike of one Deepa Nepali, but a representative struggle for the self-respect, rights, and justice of millions of Dalit youth who come to the city from remote parts of the country for opportunities and education. I express full solidarity with this movement.
Chairperson, the Rastriya Swatantra Party government, which came to power with a promise of justice and forgiveness against discrimination, does not even deem it necessary to dialogue with Deepa Nepali. This is a direct insult, discrimination, and neglect towards the entire Dalit community. This not only breaks the entire Dalit community's trust in the state but also sows the seeds of rebellion. Therefore, I strongly urge the government through the Right Honourable Chairperson to immediately hold talks with the protesting Deepa Nepali and resolve the problem. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Padam Bahadur Pariyar.
Honourable Mr. Padam Bahadur Pariyar (Nepali Congress):- Honourable Chairperson, Ganesh Nepali, who committed self-immolation on the 25th of Asar due to state involvement and helplessness, passed away on the 26th of Asar. Ganesh's family performed the cremation as per the agreement with the government, but the government has not yet implemented eight points of that agreement. It has come to my knowledge that the independent investigation commission formed as per that agreement has submitted a report that, instead of investigating, has declared Ganesh Nepali himself guilty. I want to caution the government through the Right Honourable Chairperson: what is the intention of this government to declare the deceased guilty on his own shoulders? Honourable Chairperson, through you, I want to draw the attention of the Ministry of Home Affairs: Ganesh Nepali should be declared a martyr and the agreement should be implemented.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Puja Chaudhary.
Honourable Ms. Puja Chaudhary (Janata Samajwadi Party, Nepal):- Honourable Chairperson, the incident of rape, murder, and removal of both eyes and cutting of the tongue of 3-year-old girl Garima Chaudhary, a resident of Jitpur Simara-1, has shocked and saddened us all. Everyone's heart is crying today because of this incident. This is not just about one girl and her family. How many of our daughters will continue to fall victim to such inhuman monsters and die prematurely simply because they are girls? Furthermore, if Suman Thapa, approximately 16-17 years old, and Progress Chaudhary, said to be 24 years old, are guilty of committing such heinous crimes against an innocent 3-year-old girl like Garima Chaudhary, then I demand the strictest possible punishment for such inhuman monsters through the Right Honourable Chairperson. The question of how safe children are in the name of good governance also raises questions in our minds. From Nirmala Pant to the 3-year-old girl Garima Chaudhary now, and perhaps another daughter tomorrow, therefore, through the Right Honourable Chairperson, I urge the Prime Minister and (.. time expired.)
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Manrupa Sharma.
Honourable Ms. Manrupa Sharma (Nepali Communist Party):- Honourable Chairperson, Naran Saki, who went to Dubai for carpentry work from ward number 54 of Jaljala Rural Municipality in Parbat district, died on the 30th of Shrawan last month. His body is still at the Department of Health, Dubai. I request the Nepal Government to bring the body back to Nepal as soon as possible and make a request to the concerned government and ministries. Relief should be provided to the deceased's family. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Rukmini Koirala.
Honourable Ms. Rukmini Koirala (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- Honourable Chairperson, the public hears about new budgets and new plans every year, but the reality is the same. Has the public's life changed today or not? If farmers do not get the price for their produce, how can the plan be considered successful? If youth do not get employment, how can development be achieved? If women do not feel safe, how can prosperity be said to have arrived? Therefore, I clearly urge the government that plans are needed not just on paper, but results are needed in people's homes. The country cannot be built on propaganda alone; it is necessary to abandon propaganda and adopt a focus on the basic needs of the people. It would be good for the government to move forward to protect past achievements and achieve further accomplishments, including development and construction works completed by Bhadra 22, 2082. They should be held accountable for every rupee of the public (.. time expired.)
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Renu Chand.
Honourable Ms. Renu Chand (Nepali Communist Party):- Honourable Chairperson, 3-year-old Garima Chaudhary of ward number 1 of Jitpur Simara Sub-Metropolitan City in Bara district has been raped and murdered. I want to demand from the government that the culprits be given the strictest punishment, and I have a question for the government: even though the information about the child being missing was given, why did the police not take action in time? Sometimes the Home Minister says, "Take back your vote of confidence," and it is considered a joke; sometimes, by asking the PSO, it is confirmed whether he is the Home Minister or not. Ministers are busy making jokes, busy cracking jokes; the police are also confused, asking themselves if they are police or not. And the lives of citizens are in jeopardy. The government's style of functioning and performance has become a complete joke, but the government's approach to people's lives is not a joke. Ripping out the eyes and cutting the tongue of a 3-year-old child and consuming it, it's no joke! Therefore, I want to tell the Home Minister and the Ministry that the culprits should be given the strictest punishment. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Vishnu Kumari Sapkota.
Honourable Ms. Vishnu Kumari Sapkota (Nepali Congress):- Honourable Chairperson, where is the government today? On the night of the 27th of Shrawan, landslides in Thaba Kotla, Rolpa, displaced 10 households and claimed 14 lives. Roads, bridges, and electricity are all disrupted. Although relief was announced by the government nearly 10 days ago, the citizens there have not received any form of relief. Is announcing relief the only duty of the government? If not, why can't the helicopter that goes to pick up a minister with a cold be used to deliver relief to citizens? Is this relief also to be borne by the old parties and those who have been in power for 35 years? The government cannot violate the citizens' right to food, shelter, clothing, and constitutional natural rights. I want to draw the attention of the government through the Right Honourable Chairperson. I strongly condemn the rape and subsequent murder of an innocent 3-year-old girl in Simara. Similarly, people are dying from Japanese Encephalitis; what is the government's preparation? I want to draw the attention of the government through the Right Honourable Chairperson. Thank you. Jai Nepal.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Vishnu Devi Pudasaini.
Honourable Ms. Vishnu Devi Pudasaini (Nepali Congress):- Honourable Chairperson, the extremely tragic incident of the rape and murder of a 3-year-old girl in Simara Jitpur, Bara district, has saddened all Nepalis. Such incidents are increasing day by day. In this situation, when jail sentences alone are not enough for such criminals, I draw the attention of society and the government through the Honourable House to enact laws for the strictest possible punishment. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Vishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma.
Honourable Mr. Vishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma (Nepali Communist Party:- Honourable Chairperson, when our government was not in power, it reduced its private secretariat. Now, by keeping dozens of private secretaries, private secretariats, and advisors, it is exploiting the state and misusing resources. Along with having dozens of private secretariats, dozens of types of tendencies have also been integrated, and actions that defame the government and ministers are also taking place. Therefore, I request that the dozens of private secretariats, private secretaries, and advisors be reduced, and the minister be allowed to have only one private secretary. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable members, the order of speaking during Zero Hour
concludes here. Honourable members have been received names to speak during Provincial Concerns Time based on party affiliation. I will now provide time for the Honourable members to speak. First, Honourable Member Anand Prasad Dugana, time 18 minutes. Following this, Honourable Member Vishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma.
Honourable Mr. Anand Prasad Dugana (Nepali Congress):- Chairperson, first of all, the brutal murder, not just murder, but rape and murder of a 3-year-old girl in Jitpur Simara Sub-Metropolitan City in Bara district is extremely sad and heartbreaking. Where is the government? What is the government doing? It has become difficult to say. Friends here have raised many issues during Zero Hour. The government has become irresponsible. It is not providing answers to anything. The Chairperson asked us to raise provincial issues. I don't think raising them will achieve anything. Why is the government not taking responsibility? The government does not understand its responsibility. Why did the people elect the government? Why did ministers become ministers? Why did ministers become ministers? Whether they understand their position or responsibility is unclear. Therefore, the country is in a state of being without a government, without a guardian, and orphaned. As I speak in such a situation, what I say may be many things, but I don't think anything will be fulfilled. This is not about the present. This parliamentary

We have raised our issues many times in the system. There was a practice of ministers responding to issues raised during Zero Hour, Special Time, and coming to answer. Today, that practice is gone. Because these ministers are no longer responsible. Ministers do not understand responsibility. What do ministers understand? They bring up issues from 35 years ago when they are criticized. I want to ask, did those ministers used to answer in parliament 35 years ago? Back then, they didn't just answer, they were also responsible. Therefore, are you responsible today? I want to say that. My colleagues said that a person like the Home Minister, when he goes to his constituency, says something like, 'You thought I would do this and that, but I haven't done anything.' If he hasn't done anything, he says, 'Well then, you take back your vote.' Is this responsibility? Is this what you tell the public? Is it just lip service? Is this why you became a minister? Therefore, what is seen is that people who used to run the show yesterday, people who used to dance yesterday, have become ministers and prime ministers today. This is why this situation has arisen. Therefore, I urge the government to be responsible, and the government should responsibly address the issues spoken in this parliament, as they are the issues of the people. We say the sovereign people are the people. We fought for the people. I am surprised that today this government has banned all trade unions through an ordinance. It banned student unions through an ordinance. It banned organizations. Does it want to run a non-party system? Are you trying to bring a non-party system again? If you are trying to bring a non-party system, then be prepared, we are ready again. Understand this. I want to challenge you from this rostrum. Remember yesterday, three years ago, when the movement was happening at Biratnagar Jute Mill, the government arrested BP Koirala, Manmohan Adhikari, Girija Prasad Koirala in support of the workers and kept them in Kathmandu jail on foot from Dhankuta, and they had to fast, saying they couldn't read the newspaper. After they did everything, the government had to bow down and release them. That is to say, this change happened through struggle. This change happened from student organizations. We know that when the Panchayat system was in place, after December 1, 2017 BS, when we went to study in college around 22-23 years old, we couldn't even call ourselves democrats. To call oneself a democrat meant, 'Oh, he's from Congress.' That is, a person who was called a Congress supporter either lived in India or was in jail. They couldn't live in the country. As soon as they lived in the country, they were considered anti-state. That was the situation. We have come from that situation. And you talk about 35 years? Study it! What has been done in 34 years is in writing! Where roads were built, where paths were built, where hospitals were built, where universities were built, study that. If you haven't studied, ask. By shouting '35 years, 35 years,' are you trying to minimize the work of those 34 years? If so, your own Finance Minister, Swarnim Wagle, told me one day while I was walking on the Fast Track that the economy of this country improved either when Mahesh Acharya was Finance Minister or when Ram Sharan Mahat was Finance Minister. Ask your own finance minister. When did the economy get stronger? When did development begin in this country? How much was the budget when we prepared the budget in 2047 BS, how much is the budget today? If you haven't seen the work, walk with me in my constituency, I will show you. How many works, how many schools have been built, how many primary schools have been built, how many roads have been built, how many bridges have been built, I will show you. Therefore, I urge this government to be vigilant and not to survive just by scolding. You cannot escape by scolding. You are in office with responsibility. Yesterday, when you spoke in parliament, you spoke in strong language, we know your speeches. I saw it. The Prime Minister went to Janakpur and said at a Rastriya Swatantra Party rally, 'We are the children of Madhes, you all vote for me, make me Prime Minister, if I become Prime Minister, you won't have to go to Kathmandu for your rights.' Meaning, this federalism will not last. What proposal have you seen at the Rastriya Swatantra Party convention? You have seen proposals to break federalism, so you don't have the trust of the people.' I want to say this. Therefore, one should not speak irresponsibly, nor should one act irresponsibly. After a long struggle in this country, I am talking about the CIAA. The Janjivan movement, what was it for? What was it for? For good governance, and was it not for the closure of social organizations? Did we have the right to burn Singha Durbar? Did we know we had the right to burn the court? Did we have the right to burn the President's residence? Did we have the right to burn the Parliament building? Did we have the right to burn the CIAA? Did we have the right to burn the Special Court? Did we have the right to burn the houses of police organizations across the country, which were built for security? No. Then you burned them. Why? Out of anger? If it was done out of personal anger, then say so. You burned the houses of leaders. Those who struggled for democracy, for the people's democracy in this country, Rana exiled them from the country. Krishna Prasad Koirala died in jail. If you don't have this information, get it. When their houses were burned, didn't you feel even a little bit that I am a democrat or that I have worked against democracy, against people's democracy? Therefore, you are involved in the same trend as the incident that happened in Bara recently, why deny it? Why deny it? Therefore, I want to say that the current situation is not good for the country. Nationalism is weak. Nationalism is so weak. I said this on this rostrum before as well, that as long as nationalism is not strengthened, there are fears that nothing can be achieved in this country. You must have seen, when Alexander came to India, what did he do? He first destroyed the temples there, destroyed the culture, destroyed the language. In the time of the British, a person was called 'Sir', implying intelligence. A person called 'Mahashay' was considered to have weak intellect. Are we like that anywhere now? We are still like that. Therefore, any ruler, to rule, to enslave, implements their own tendencies. Yes, that is the situation we are in now. I feel that yesterday, for this country, BP Koirala used to say, if I had only talked about democracy, the Nepali people would not have had to suffer on December 1, 2017 BS. If I had only talked about nationalism, they would not have had to suffer on December 1, 2017 BS. I took nationalism and democracy together, and therefore, the Nepali people had to suffer, we had to suffer, we had to live in shoes, we had to live in jail. Did Durga Subedi really not hang in 25 years? Did Yagya Bahadur Thapa, Bhim Narayan Shrestha not get shot? Did Saroj Prasad Koirala and Tej Bahadur Amatya not get shot? Similarly, did leaders of various parties not get shot? You are sitting in the chair you are in today to fulfill the dreams of those martyrs. You are not sitting there to scold them. If you are sitting there to scold them, then you are not worthy of the chair. I want to say this in plain language. Therefore, I say, in the current situation, trade unions! Was it wrong for trade unions to go and agitate at Biratnagar Jute Mill? What was the workers' movement by the Trade Union Congress at Biratnagar Jute Mill for? It was not just a workers' movement; it was a movement to dismantle the autocratic rule. Those who went to jail for their organizations around 25, 26, 27 BS, fought, were shot at Kamdaha Mandal Yadukoha school, what was that for? It was not just about the right to study in school; it was also a fight for democracy. It was about democracy. Therefore, if you are trying to bring a non-party system by banning that today, you should not even dream of it. Therefore, I want to say that this is the situation the country is in. I have doubts here. I feel that it has been 56 years since I went to jail, was kicked out, kicked the jail gate. Coming from that situation, the country has now gone into the hands of others. If the country descends into anarchy, becomes Afghanistan or Sudan, who will be responsible? Who will be responsible? We will be responsible. We, who are sitting in this house as representatives, are raising our issues. We can say with pride, we can tell this government, you cannot do this, you cannot do that. If we cannot say this, then we should also resign and leave as incompetent. But I want to say, who knows when peacekeeping forces might come here. It's already difficult for foreign troops. What is this in the name of peacekeeping forces? Why did that incident happen in Kaptanaganj? Why did the Home Minister go after four days? If he had gone at the beginning, the incident in Siraha might not have happened. People might not have died in Golbazar. The child might not have been beaten in Janakpur. It wouldn't have been necessary to impose a curfew in Parsa. All these incidents have arisen because the government has acted irresponsibly and irresponsibly. I feel that the force that caused the incidents on the 23rd and 24th has not yet had its wishes fulfilled. Therefore, we need to be vigilant and discuss these matters. The time for scolding each other is over. Leaders who fought for democracy, for people's democracy, scolding? You scold me, I scold you? Where will we live? Where will we stay? It was said that this will become Sri Lanka, this will become Bangladesh, millions will be affected, leaders said this at the rostrum! They said it, where are those people today? What has happened? Therefore, before we scold anyone, we must look in the mirror. Where am I? When I say someone's face is black, smeared with black, I must think whether my face is smeared with black or not? Is my face pure or clean or not? I must think about that myself, don't I? Therefore, what I see is that the situation in this country is not easy and not good anywhere. Today, in the name of the landless, why were the landless brought here? They say there will be floods. Now these landless people have been placed in one place, now they are being moved to another place. And they are told to pay 25,000, 14,000 rupees and find accommodation on rent! What does that mean? It means that no matter what, you are causing so much suffering, and then people will start saying, 'Remove your hands and leave,' and they will end up begging. This is the situation being created for the landless. Now, a person like the Prime Minister says, 'Nepalis have also encroached on Indian land.' What is he saying? What does he want to say? Oh! Are you trying to abandon Lipulekh, Limpiyadhura, Kalapani? They have encroached on our land, and our people have also encroached on their land, so let's leave both, and it will be equal. Therefore, a person like the Prime Minister should not say such things when answering questions. The answer to the question must be given correctly, purely.

Please give it for the good of the country, for the good of democracy, for the good of democracy. The Home Minister comes and threatens the House, saying, 'Don't ask such questions.' Coincidentally, I wasn't there that day, otherwise, there would have been a real fight. This is not the way. We are the ones who should ask questions, the children of the people should ask questions. The questions asked in this parliament are the questions asked by the people. We are here, accountable to the people. If we cannot convey the people's concerns, why should the people vote for us? Why should the people vote for us? Therefore, what happens is that all these things, especially on the day he said in the House of Representatives, 'Nepalis have also encroached on Indian land,' the very next day, the Indian army stopped the embankment we were building in Susta. Look at what is happening in Susta now? People from Susta are coming here and crying. They are sitting at Maitighar. It's like playing a flute in front of a buffalo; if the buffalo doesn't dance, it doesn't matter. The people are crying, the people are wailing, the people are screaming, the people are fasting, the government doesn't care. What kind of government is this? I don't think yesterday's government was so irresponsible. If we stood up and said something or spoke once to yesterday's government, the government would investigate and respond. Today, colleagues have said that this happened in Rukum, this happened in Jajarkot, this has also happened in Magdi, villages have been swept away by floods. But I don't know if the government knows. But the government should come to this rostrum responsibly and say, 'This is happening in the country, this is being done in the country, so many people have died in the floods, the honorable member said yesterday that relief has not been provided in the country, he said correctly. The government doesn't have time to deliver relief to the country, but when a minister falls ill, it sends a helicopter, goes by helicopter... (Time expired). Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma, your time is up (13:52). Next, Honorable Member Rukmini Koirala. Honorable Mr. Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma (Communist Party of Nepal): (13:52) Honorable Chairperson, today I want to offer some suggestions to the government and briefly discuss the development and issues of my constituency. Firstly, it is believed that the cultural tradition in our country began in 463 BC. The development of cultural development, both physical and intangible, is believed to have begun with the birth of Gautam Buddha in Lumbini and the time of Kirat King Yalambar. Although thousands of years have passed, the process of modern development has not been long. The five-year plan for modern development was implemented from 2013 BS, and the country's development could not gain momentum due to the absolute rule of the kings, the looting by the royal family, and the exclusive rule of the courtiers and mandales. The development of modern and digital technology came much later. The process of modern and digital development is considered to have begun only after the campaign of computers in every home and mobiles in every hand by the government formed after the peace process following the people's war between the government and the rebels. The establishment of a democratic republic of Nepal has made the people free and dignified. Roads, electricity, communication, physical infrastructure, health, education, and food facilities have reached villages, although there are now more complexities, inconveniences, and emerging issues, and the public is worried. Honorable Chairperson, old parties could not do it, we can do it, old parties could not say it, we say it - believing in YouTube propaganda, the people gave immense votes. Has the government, established as the center of people's hope and trust, been able to become the center of people's hope and trust? I want to ask the government a question. What have the people received from budget formulation to displacement? This must be the new good governance that the old ones couldn't provide, right? The good governance of the new is displacement, entering the era of servitude, the death and suicide of 11 landless people, the self-immolation of 5 youths, reaching the level of violation of Nepal's constitution, human rights, and international standards - this is the good governance of the new, this is what has been seen. Where has the prosperity of the country and the people reached? I want to ask a question. Where has our country's economy reached? The main indicator of the country's economy is the stock market. Today, even in the season, the condition of the stock market is dire. When trust and confidence cannot be given in development, capital flight has already begun. When capital flees, we lose employment, the state loses revenue, and the country faces great damage. The sky-high price of food, the artificial scarcity of gas, making the country helpless, allowing destruction, arbitrary arrests, detentions, cancellations, and appointments based on orders, and the state's involvement in intimidating some by offering impunity in the name of money laundering, is becoming a topic of widespread discussion. Honorable Chairperson, it is a tragedy that the country is being run based on the status of the Prime Minister and his private secretariat. The government should be accountable to the House and the people, but it seems that no authority is accountable. Because there is no sign of the Prime Minister's anti-national statements being corrected. This has already proven the Prime Minister himself a failure. The controversial appointment of ambassadors, passport printing, transfer, promotion, and posting of employees - where has the government reached? Where has it taken us? Perhaps it has made a laughing stock of itself. How far has the Air Service Corporation's rot reached? The government's intentions are clearly exposed. The appointment of a subordinate by disregarding the number one person has made the country a laughing stock. This is the failure of a government defeated by the Supreme Court, which has overturned the minister's excesses. After becoming a failed entity, those chosen by the people should know when to step down. I want to ask the government again, what is the status of the BYD vehicles that the government has forcibly and verbally legalized? The customs department has further confirmed that the main objective was tax evasion, and you must have received the report of 150 million in tax evasion for smuggling illegal vehicles. This is your crime and failure. Today, you have withdrawn the education tax, health tax, electricity tax, and death tax! This is another failure of yours and the government's. The inability to bear the burden of the people, saying 'take your vote,' is also another failure. This tendency is political poverty. Honorable Chairperson, the world community and imperialist powers, unable to confront China, are trying to use Nepal's land to encircle and destroy China. Why are some educational institutions and even government officials eager to celebrate the birthday of the Dalai Lama, a person with no interest in Nepal? Whom are they serving? The government should investigate those who cultivate foreign investment, create rifts in Nepal-China relations, and try to make Nepal a battlefield for foreign powers like the arms trade and TOBY, and send them to China to do politics. Honorable Chairperson, according to the National Census 2078, out of the 165 directly elected constituencies, 10 constituencies have a Dalit population of more than 25%. Baglung 2 has 33%, Achham 2 has 39%, Dailekh 2 has 30.2%, Jajarkot has 29.1%, Kalikot has 28.3%, Parbat has 26.3%, Magdi 9 has 26.9%, Achham 9 has 25.9%, Saptari 3 has 25.6%, Saptari 4 has 25% population. In total, there is a population of 4 million in Nepal. It is a tragedy that this large population, working in every village and settlement, has not yet been able to exercise the fundamental rights guaranteed by the constitution. I urge the government to be serious about this. Honorable Chairperson, many countries in history have launched great campaigns to make our country economically prosperous and powerful. By calling upon the citizens, they have increased working hours and, through excessive labor, have made their country the happiest and most prosperous country in the world. South Korea, devastated by war and plagued by extreme poverty in the 1950s, requested its citizens to work tirelessly for 60 hours a week and, through the miracle of the Han River, made the country and its people prosperous in a short time. Today, it has become a destination for employment for Nepalis and youth from other countries. The Japanese people worked day and night to rebuild and make Japan prosperous after World War II. Due to the hard work of the Japanese government and people, Japan has become the world's top economic power, and the people have transformed into a happy nation. Today, it has become a place of labor for workers from countries like Nepal. Germany, devastated in World War II, called upon its citizens to build the country. They adopted the 'Economic Miracle' policy for economic prosperity, worked hard for a long time, and increased economic growth and productivity. They made their country powerful. Honorable Chairperson, a small country with no natural resources and means is making its country an economic center and prosperous country in the world by making its citizens work hard for a long time. The incredible development of China today, which has gone through the pain of war and colonialism, is also possible due to the long and hard work of the country's citizens and government. It is possible due to working 12 hours a day, 6 days a week. China has succeeded in achieving modern and incredible development in the world through tireless hard work. The prosperous countries and their citizens in the Gulf, such as the UAE and Qatar, have achieved this through long hours of hard work. It has become a destination for labor for the infrastructure development and economic prosperity of our country, attracting both foreign and domestic workers. There is no history of any country or individual becoming prosperous without working hard day and night. Only by involving the citizens in the great campaign of nation-building and working hard for a long time can we become powerful. Our country's government should learn these good lessons from prosperous countries. It seems determined for rulers to become kings by displacing the people and making them beggars. Other countries rebuilt war-torn and destroyed nations and saved their countries. The youth of our country have destroyed their own country. They have destroyed the nation and nationality. Today, that is not enough, it is not visible. They are enjoying themselves by giving two more holidays. Instead of working day and night to build the country that has been turned to ashes, they are wasting time enjoying themselves, and it seems two days of holiday have been given. It has become the country that gives the most holidays in the world, for ringing bells in temples, for sleeping with bottles on random days. This tendency will never uplift the country. sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Honorable Member Shri Krishna Prasad Adhikari draws the government's attention to the impact of recent heavy rains and landslides on various districts of Bagmati Province, urging for rehabilitation and relocation of displaced people. He also highlights the potential of Bagmati Province in tourism, agriculture, and hydropower if the government implements proper policies. He criticizes the government's current path of arbitrariness and inefficiency, its suppression of the press, and its perceived attempts to undermine federalism and constitutional principles. He points out the lack of transparency in appointments and the government's actions against landless squatters. He further discusses the rising inflation, shortage of essential goods like gas and passports, and the lack of support for farmers. He also criticizes the government's priorities in disaster response and its insensitivity to public issues and national values. He questions the government's reliance on popularity and algorithms. He raises concerns about the plight of Nepali migrant workers, including exploitation by agencies, lack of job security, and the increasing number of deaths and suicides abroad, demanding government data and action.

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Honorable Member Rekha Kumari Jha discusses the challenges faced by provincial governments in Nepal's federal system, stating that they lack sufficient authority, resources, and administrative capacity despite the adoption of federalism. She argues that the concentration of power with the federal government hinders provincial governments from effectively serving their constituents and fulfilling their responsibilities. She calls for the federal government to fully transfer constitutionally mandated rights and resources to the provinces and to expedite the creation of necessary laws for provincial functioning.

The Finance Minister assured that the government would facilitate the process if studies and decisions were made according to law and indicated a positive approach towards legalization for medicinal purposes.
